thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — cache-routing error surge detected for multiple tenants, elevated 5xx and stale-response reports. Auto-page sent to oncall. Rule: cache-router v2 returning mismatched shard mappings. Root TS=1840502468

alisa: I'm oncall — looking. Can someone post current scope (tenants, error classes, regions)?

ben: Error spike visible since 1840502100. 5xx rate up ~8x for model-backend requests where routing used the recent cache-routing table. Affected: acme-inc, beta-app, internal-test. Regions: us-west1 primarily. Errors are 502 from reverse-proxy because requests forwarded to drained workers. Also a small set of corrupted cached keys returning stale model config => correctness problems.

maria: Confirming some evals show model prompts getting wrong system tokens when cache path used. This is causing customer-visible hallucinations in a tiny cohort. Severity: correctness for a handful of tenants.

tao: Support: acme-inc reported "we're getting weird answers, sometimes older model versions". They're seeing it on 3% of calls (non-negligible). They escalated to customer-SRE.

ben: Quick mitigation options: 1) disable cache-routing v2 and roll back to v1 mapping, 2) apply per-tenant cache-bypass for affected tenants, 3) traffic-shape requests that matched v2 mapping to reduce load. My recommendation: immediate per-tenant bypass + traffic throttle for routed traffic while we prepare rollback.

alisa: Agreed. Ben, apply per-tenant bypass for acme-inc and beta-app. Chao, can you take handoff for rolling back mapping if bypass doesn't stabilize?

chao: Taking it. I'll stand up the rollback plan. Ben — push the bypass and throttle playbook. Post commands here.

ben: Running bypass now — using admin CLI.

ben: ```
# bypass cache-routing for tenant acme-inc and beta-app
redwoodctl cache routing set-bypass --tenant acme-inc --reason "stale-routing v2" --duration 1h
redwoodctl cache routing set-bypass --tenant beta-app --reason "stale-routing v2" --duration 1h
```

ben: Also applying soft throttle on route-group to limit any noisy fanout while we observe: ```
redwoodctl traffic shape apply --route-group cache-router-v2 --max-rps 80 --burst 200 --reason "mitigation 1840502468"
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: traffic-shape-config -> staging -> prod. CI checks passed. Started rollout to us-west1. (deploy id: dpl-1840502480)

chao: Watching rollout. If we still see >1% correctness errors after bypass + throttle for 5m, I'll cut the v2->v1 mapping rollback.

maria: Monitoring evals. Pre-mitigation: acme-inc correctness failures ~3.2%. After bypass (t+40s): sampling shows down to 0.4% for acme-inc. Good signal but need longer tail.

tao: Notified acme SRE and product — letting them know we applied bypass and throttle, will update in 10m. They asked for ETA to full fix.

ben: Observability: 5xxs dropped from 220/min -> 18/min after throttle + bypass. Latency for bypassed requests increased slightly (prefix cache miss) but within SLO.

alisa: Great. Chao — proceed with rollback plan in 10m unless we see recurrence. Document commands you'll run.

chao: Rollback plan (manual gate): 1) set routing dry-run to v1 mapping 2) run canary 100 req/s for 2m 3) if stable, promote to 100% 4) invalidate any inconsistent cache partitions. Commands: ```
# dry-run v1 mapping
redwoodctl cache routing set-mapping --version v1 --mode dry-run --reason "rollback check"
# promote after checks
redwoodctl cache routing set-mapping --version v1 --mode active --reason "emergency-rollback"
# invalidate suspect cache partitions
redwoodctl cache partition invalidate --partitions "shard-7,shard-8" --reason "corrupt-entries"
```

incident-bot: Update: mitigation applied by ben. State=mitigating. Pager duty acknowledged by alisa.

ben: Small snag: one of the invalidation jobs hit rate-limit in orchestration service, retrying with backoff and chunking. Logs: ```
[2028-07-04T14:07:10Z] invalidate-job: rate limit response 429 from orchestrator
[2028-07-04T14:07:15Z] retrying chunk 3/12 after 2s
```

maria: Running deeper sample: acme-inc production traces show requested model version matches expected on 99.6% of calls now. Customer ROI calls look normal.

tao: Acme SRE responded: "thanks, seeing improvement. We'll keep monitoring and will update if anything pops up."

chao: Beginning dry-run of v1 mapping now. Canary traffic running (100r/s). Observing for 3m.

ben: Metrics during canary: 5xx rate steady low, error-rate for canary <0.1%. No regressions in latency.

chao: Promoting v1 mapping to active. ```
redwoodctl cache routing set-mapping --version v1 --mode active --reason "promote after mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: mapping-change applied: map-v1 active in us-west1. (deploy id: dpl-1840502901)

maria: After promote: correctness failures for acme-inc back to baseline 0.02%. 5xx back to normal.

alisa: Closing mitigation. We'll keep extended monitoring for 1h and then open a postmortem. Ben, Chao, Maria, Tao — will coordinate on the incident write-up. Action items: - root cause triage (runtime routing table validation) - add automatic canary dry-run for mapping changes - improve invalidation job retry/backoff - customer comms follow-up with acme.

ben: Filing follow-ups in incident board now.

incident-bot: Incident state -> resolved-mitigated. Duration 11m. :white_check_mark:

tao: I'll send a short note to acme SRE summarizing what we did and next steps.

alisa: Thanks team. Good coordination.

ben: Quick note for postmortem — the mapping push didn't have a preflight check for drained-worker tags. We'll add that to the release checklist.

chao: I'll file the rollback playbook as a runbook entry.

maria: I'll attach eval examples showing the failure modes to the postmortem so product can see the customer impact sample queries.

incident-bot: Thread closed for updates — open if anything else crops up.
